mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a strong underlying recovery trend that will continue to drive further gains over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, as evidenced by its steady increase, will continue to drive more people into urban centers, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as commuting patterns solidify.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, despite WORKPLACES mobility rising by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: As people spend less time at home (RESIDENTIAL decreasing) and increasingly utilize public transport (TRANSIT increasing), their propensity for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, will rise significantly over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to decrease and TRANSIT continues to increase.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signals a broader return to pre-pandemic routines and confidence in public spaces, which will collectively drive an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT showing continued recovery trends.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant increase in PARKS mobility suggests a growing public comfort with outdoor activities. If this comfort is maintained, it will translate into a general willingness to engage in other out-of-home activities, including retail, over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains above 30% change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next week, even if PARKS mobility remains above 30% change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility combined with a further decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, if it occurs, would indicate a shift away from local essential trips without a corresponding increase in discretionary spending, leading to a decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -18% AND RESIDENTIAL falls below 15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks, despite GROCERY_PHARM falling below -18% and RESIDENTIAL falling below 15%.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a sustained trend of people spending less time at home, directly freeing up time and opportunity for engagement in retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing to decrease.

mechanism_narrative: As summer progresses (mid-July), the combined effect of increased outdoor leisure (PARKS mobility) and reduced time spent at home (RESIDENTIAL mobility) will create a strong seasonal impetus for increased discretionary out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite PARKS mobility remaining high and RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing to decrease.
